chapter: Algiers parades and the wider city
title: Algiers and New Orleans as one city; Rampart Street cabarets
summary: Algiers saw itself as part of one city; he remembers Rampart Street and the blue light district cabarets where string bands worked.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: In the old days, did you all think of it as the Algiers as one city and another city over across the river, or all just like one big city?

Well, we knew it was all one big city, you know. It's different ones like Jefferson Powers and Algiers, but that was different than that, you know. But like New Orleans, you know, over here, we always think we're the one city. Yeah.

And over there, they talk a lot about like downtown sometimes and uptown. Some of the downtown people never did get across Canal Street. They say, well, they're like... Well, you got people right down there now.

I know some family that have never seen the river. Really? On and raised here. That's right. Haven't seen the river. And they haven't been nowhere. The only one thing they've been downtown. They were ripe age, you know, and some of them died. And I seen people down there, live down there. Old people told me they never seen the Congo Parade. Live farther down, you know. Yeah. Like around the Ninth Ward all down there. Yeah. Well, it was just during that time, it was just like a country down there on the other side of Duster Canal. Yeah. You take like right down on the other side of Lafayette Street down there. See, used to be a canal there. Used to build, yeah. Used to bring charcoal and product in there, you know, for more of the lake. It was just like the new basin there. That was the old basin down there. Yeah. I remember that. Yeah. Well, that's the time there. That's where my name was playing on that old cabaretts down there on Rampart Street. That was the blue light district all down there during that time. Katie White and all that. Yeah. That's why they had all those cabaretts all in there. And that's why, I tell you, that's what was work was over there, you see, for the band. Yeah. Nothing but string band. That's all. That's that Dixie band, Dixieland style. That's all it is.
That'd be in the dance hall.

Well, it's, yeah. Well, you see, you drink in the ball and you have a little place to go in the back where you dance. Uh-huh. That's where the band was all around in that place. That's all it was. Well, there wasn't too much uptime. It was around the press part of the town. That's where the moister was kept.
